title: Regression With No Suspect
objective: Diagnose why the hot loop regressed by inspecting counters and running counterfactuals, then commit to exactly one root cause.
briefing:
A routine profiling pass shows the hot loop of your rollup-worker service has regressed measurably since yesterday's build.

The change list mentions a data-layout tweak and a library bump, neither of which touches this loop's code path.

The machine has a 32 KiB, 64 B-line, 8-way cache where the loop lives. Nothing else changed.

Profiling reruns are expensive: you have a fixed budget of probes before you must commit.

actions.label: Read perf counters
actions.description: Cycle estimates: current build vs known-good baseline.

actions.label: Dump cache configuration
actions.description: Size / line / associativity of each level.

actions.label: Miss-rate timeline
actions.description: Miss rate across eight windows of the run.

actions.label: Set & line analysis
actions.description: Where misses land across sets; churn among hot lines; locality metrics.

actions.label: Coherence probe
actions.description: Cross-core invalidations vs local writes; same-word conflicts.

actions.label: Prefetch audit
actions.description: Prefetches issued vs used under current policy.

hypotheses.label: Spatial locality loss
hypotheses.detail: The access pattern jumps across memory instead of walking it; every cache line is used once instead of many times, multiplying traffic without exceeding capacity.

hypotheses.label: Cache set conflicts
hypotheses.detail: The hot lines now map onto one cache set; associativity cannot hold them, so each pass evicts the line the next iteration needs.

hypotheses.label: Cold-data churn
hypotheses.detail: The loop walks fresh data every pass instead of reusing anything; nearly every access is a first-touch miss even though nothing exceeds capacity.

hypotheses.label: True sharing on hot data
hypotheses.detail: Both cores genuinely write the same shared word; coherence transfers are inherent to the algorithm but their volume exploded with the write mix change.

solution.explanation: Both cores genuinely write the same shared word; coherence transfers are inherent to the algorithm but their volume exploded with the write mix change.
